<b>ВИЧ</b> (вирус иммунодефицита человек: HIV (human immunodeficiency virus) attacks CD4 lymphocytes. It is transmitted through sex without a condom, through blood (shared needles) and from mother to child. It may cause no symptoms for years; without treatment it leads to AIDS. Modern antiretroviral therapy allows people to live full lives, and a person with an undetectable viral load does not pass the virus to a partner. Pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is available.
<b>Вирус папилломы человека</b> — самая: Human papillomavirus is the most common STI. Most often it clears on its own, but some types cause genital warts, and the oncogenic types (16, 18) cause cancer of the cervix, throat and other organs. There is an effective vaccine, best given before the start of sexual activity; women are advised to have regular screening (cytology, HPV test).
<b>Вирус простого герпеса</b> (ВПГ-2 и В: Herpes simplex virus (HSV-2 and HSV-1) causes painful blisters. After infection it stays in the nerve ganglia for life and flares up from time to time. Medication shortens flare-ups and lowers the risk of transmission.
<b>Хламидиоз</b> — бактериальная инфекци: Chlamydia is a bacterial infection, often without symptoms (especially in women). Untreated, it can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility. It is treated with antibiotics; both partners must be treated.
<b>Гонорея</b> — бактерия-диплококк. Выз: Gonorrhea is caused by a diplococcus bacterium. It causes discharge and pain on urination, but can also be silent. It is treated with antibiotics; resistance to them is growing, so self-treatment is not an option.
<b>Сифилис</b> вызывает спиралевидная ба: Syphilis is caused by a spiral-shaped bacterium. First comes a painless sore, then a rash, then a latent stage; untreated, it damages the heart, blood vessels and nervous system. It responds well to penicillin. Testing is by a blood test.
<b>Гепатит B</b> поражает печень, переда: Hepatitis B damages the liver; it is transmitted through blood and sexually, can become chronic and lead to cirrhosis and liver cancer. There is a vaccine, which is part of the national immunization schedule.
<b>Половое влечение (либидо)</b> рождает: Sexual desire (libido) arises from the interplay of the brain and hormones. The hypothalamus and pituitary control the gonads, and their hormones (testosterone, estrogens) return to the brain and make it more sensitive to cues; the dopamine system creates motivation, while the prefrontal cortex weighs the situation and makes decisions. The strength of desire is highly individual and changes with age, health, mood and relationships; a lack of desire (asexuality) is also a normal variant, as long as it does not bother the person. Choose a state.
<b>Инфекции, передающиеся половым путём: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs). Many of them run without symptoms for a long time, so a person may not know they are infected and may pass the infection on. Protection: condoms, vaccines (HPV, hepatitis B), regular testing and treatment of both partners, HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis. Click a pathogen.
<b>Контрацепция</b> — способы предотврат:
Contraception means ways to prevent an unwanted pregnancy. The bar height shows how many women out of 100 become pregnant within a year with typical (not perfect) use of the method. A green ring means the method also protects against STIs: of all methods, only the condom does this. It is best to discuss the choice of method with a gynecologist.

Consent. Any sexual contact is possible only with the voluntary, informed consent of both partners, which can be withdrawn at any moment. Everyone has the right to say “no”. The law protects minors: in Russia the age of consent is 16.

\n <div><h2>Три системы по Хелен Фи:
Helen Fisher’s three systems

  • Lust (sex hormones) — a general drive for intimacy.
  • Attraction/romantic love (dopamine, norepinephrine) — focus on one person.
  • Attachment (oxytocin, vasopressin) — a long-term bond and trust.

When to see a doctor

Discharge, sores, rash, itching, pain on urination, or unprotected contact with a new partner are reasons to get tested for STIs (this can be done anonymously). A persistent decrease or loss of desire that troubles the person is a reason to see an endocrinologist, gynecologist, urologist or sexologist.

\n <div><h2>Ферменты</h2>\n:
Enzymes

Enzymes are biological catalysts made of protein. Three properties set them apart from other catalysts: enormous efficiency, strict specificity and the capacity for regulation.

Simple enzymes consist of protein only (pepsin, amylase, lipase). Conjugated enzymes consist of a protein part (the apoenzyme) and a non-protein cofactor: either tightly bound — a prosthetic group (metal ions, heme) — or an easily detached coenzyme (most often a vitamin derivative). Together they form the holoenzyme.

How an enzyme speeds up a reaction

An enzyme does not change the energy of the starting materials or products, but it lowers the activation energy — the barrier that must be overcome (graph on the right). Mechanisms: precise orientation of the substrate (binding at a minimum of three points), strain on its bonds, acid–base catalysis (like Glu35 and Asp52 of lysozyme, or the histidine of many enzymes) and covalent catalysis.

Michaelis–Menten stages: E + S ⇄ ES → ES* → EP → E + P.

Specificity

  • Absolute — a single substrate (arginase → arginine only).
  • Relative — a group of similar substrates (lipase — all fats, pepsin — proteins).
  • Stereospecificity — only one isomer (L- or D-).
  • Reaction specificity: from histidine, histidase makes a keto acid, while a decarboxylase makes histamine.

<b>Конкурентный ингибитор</b> (красные ш: A competitive inhibitor (red spheres) resembles the substrate and occupies the active site. The more substrate there is, the less often the inhibitor manages to bind: at high [S] the rate still reaches Vmax, but Km increases. This is how allopurinol (for gout), statins, methotrexate and neostigmine work.
<b>Неконкурентный ингибитор</b> (фиолето: A noncompetitive inhibitor (purple) does not resemble the substrate; it binds elsewhere on the enzyme and changes its shape. Excess substrate does not help: Vmax falls, while Km stays the same. Heavy-metal ions act this way on the SH groups of enzymes; allosteric feedback inhibition by an end product also belongs here.
<b>Необратимый ингибитор</b> (оранжевые): An irreversible inhibitor (orange) attaches to the enzyme by a covalent bond — the enzyme is out of action for good (dark models). Activity returns only when new enzyme molecules are synthesized. Examples: cyanide (cytochrome oxidase), sarin and organophosphate poisons (cholinesterase), aspirin (cyclooxygenase), penicillin (bacterial transpeptidase).
<b>Денатурация.</b> Выше ~45 °C белок-фе: Denaturation. Above ~45 °C the enzyme protein loses its shape (the gray models tremble and unfold), the active site falls apart and the reaction almost stops. This is why a body temperature above 41–42 °C is dangerous.
<b>Холод.</b> Молекулы движутся медленне: Cold. Molecules move more slowly and collide less often: the rate falls roughly by half for every 10 °C. But the enzyme is not destroyed — when warmed, it comes back to life (this is the basis for freezing food and organs).

<b>Скорость реакции</b> растёт с концент: The reaction rate rises with substrate concentration [S] as long as free enzymes are available. When all active sites are occupied (yellow lights), saturation sets in — the rate reaches Vmax. Km (the Michaelis constant) is the concentration at which the rate is half of maximum: the lower the Km, the more strongly the enzyme “likes” its substrate. This is the Michaelis–Menten equation: v = Vmax·[S] / (Km + [S]).

\n <div><h2>От чего зависит скорост:
What the rate depends on

Substrate concentration. At low [S] the rate rises almost linearly; at high [S] it levels off at Vmax: all enzymes are occupied (saturation). Km equals the [S] at which v = ½ Vmax; it is inversely related to the enzyme’s affinity for the substrate.

Temperature. Up to the optimum (~37–40 °C) the rate roughly doubles for every 10 °C; above 45–50 °C the protein denatures (thermolability).

pH. Each enzyme has its own optimum: pepsin works in the acidic stomach (pH 1.5–2), trypsin in the slightly alkaline intestine (~8). When gastric juice is not acidic enough, pepsin digests proteins poorly.

Enzyme concentration — the rate is directly proportional to it. Units of activity: 1 IU = 1 µmol of substrate per 1 min; 1 katal = 1 mol per 1 s.

Inhibitors

Reversible inhibitors bind by weak bonds: competitive (substrate analogs, ↑Km) and noncompetitive (bind elsewhere, ↓Vmax). Irreversible inhibitors form a covalent bond — they are often poisons. In Lineweaver–Burk coordinates (1/v vs 1/[S]) the curve becomes a straight line: a competitive inhibitor changes its slope but not its intercept on the 1/v axis, while a noncompetitive inhibitor raises that intercept.

<b>Аллостерическая регуляция.</b> Регуля: Allosteric regulation. A regulatory enzyme is built from several subunits. Besides the active sites, it has an allosteric site (the ring in the middle) for an effector molecule that does not resemble the substrate. The subunits influence one another: occupying one site makes it easier to occupy the next (cooperativity) — so the rate curve is not a hyperbola but an S-shaped curve. An activator (here AMP — the “low energy” signal) shifts the curve to the left, an inhibitor (ATP — “plenty of energy”) shifts it to the right. This is how phosphofructokinase controls glycolysis. Move [S] and choose an effector.
<b>Фосфорилирование</b> — самый частый в: Phosphorylation is the most common switch for enzymes. A protein kinase transfers phosphate from ATP to a serine, threonine or tyrosine of a protein, and a phosphatase removes it with water. On the left is the real Src tyrosine kinase (PDB 2SRC, domains in different colors). The phosphate on its tail (Tyr527, orange light) latches into the “pocket” of the SH2 domain and keeps the enzyme switched off; an ATP analog lies in the blue catalytic domain. On the right is fat-cell lipase: phosphate from a kinase switches it on (epinephrine → fat breakdown). Glycogen synthase is the opposite: it is active without phosphate.
<b>Частичный протеолиз.</b> Многие проте: Partial proteolysis. Many proteases are synthesized as inactive proenzymes (zymogens) so that they do not digest their own cell. Cleaving off part of the chain (light peptide) changes the shape of the protein: the new N-terminus (Ile16) tucks inside and “assembles” the active site — the catalytic triad His57, Asp102, Ser195 (lights). This is how trypsinogen → trypsin (by enteropeptidase in the gut), pepsinogen → pepsin (by hydrochloric acid) and the clotting factors are switched on. The model shows factor Xa (PDB 1IQJ) with an anticoagulant in the active site.
<b>Изоферменты</b> — разные формы одного: Isoenzymes are different forms of the same enzyme. Lactate dehydrogenase is a tetramer built from two types of subunits: H (heart, blue) and M (muscle and liver, red). The five combinations give LDH1 (H4) … LDH5 (M4); they move differently in an electric field. Normally LDH2 > LDH1. In myocardial infarction, LDH1 leaks from the heart muscle and its peak overtakes LDH2; in liver damage, LDH5 rises. Such “marker” enzymes are the basis of enzyme diagnostics.

\n <div><h2>Способы регуляции</h2><:
Modes of regulation

  • Allosteric — effectors at a special site; often by feedback: the end product of a pathway inhibits its first enzyme.
  • Cofactors — a quarter of enzymes need metal ions (Mg²⁺, Zn²⁺, Fe²⁺, Cu²⁺, Mn²⁺ and others).
  • Partial proteolysis — proenzyme → enzyme (irreversible).
  • Phosphorylation / dephosphorylation — protein kinases and phosphatases, fast and reversible.
  • Association and dissociation of subunits.
  • Change in the amount of enzyme — synthesis and breakdown (hours).

Enzymes in medicine

Enzymopathies are inherited diseases caused by a defective enzyme (phenylketonuria, galactosemia). Enzyme therapy uses enzymes and their inhibitors as drugs: pancreatic enzymes for pancreatic insufficiency, protease inhibitors for pancreatitis. Enzyme diagnostics measures blood enzymes (ALT, AST, CK-MB, amylase, LDH, alkaline phosphatase) and uses pure enzymes as reagents to measure glucose, cholesterol and urea.

<b>Витамин B1 (тиамин).</b> Кофермент —: Vitamin B1 (thiamine). Its coenzyme is thiamine pyrophosphate: it is needed by enzymes that remove CO₂ from keto acids (pyruvate dehydrogenase, α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase) and by transketolase. Without it, nerve tissue, which runs on glucose, starves. Deficiency causes beriberi (polyneuritis, weakness, heart failure), and in people with alcoholism, Wernicke–Korsakoff syndrome. Sources: grain husks, yeast, pork, legumes.
<b>Витамин B2 (рибофлавин)</b> — жёлтый: Vitamin B2 (riboflavin) is a yellow pigment. Its forms FMN and FAD are the prosthetic groups of flavoproteins: succinate dehydrogenase of the Krebs cycle, acyl-CoA dehydrogenase of β-oxidation, complex I of the respiratory chain. The flavin ring accepts two hydrogen atoms at once. Deficiency: cracks at the corners of the mouth (angular stomatitis), cheilitis, glossitis, eye inflammation. Sources: milk, eggs, liver.
<b>Витамин PP (B3, ниацин)</b> — никотин: Vitamin PP (B3, niacin) is nicotinic acid and nicotinamide. It is part of NAD⁺ and NADP⁺, the hydrogen (hydride ion) carriers for hundreds of dehydrogenases: glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, β-oxidation, fat synthesis. A little niacin is made from tryptophan (≈60 mg Trp → 1 mg). Deficiency causes pellagra, the disease of the “three Ds”: dermatitis, diarrhea, dementia. Sources: meat, fish, peanuts, mushrooms.
<b>Витамин B5 (пантотеновая кислота</b>,: Vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid, from Greek “pantos” — everywhere) is part of coenzyme A: the SH group at its end (yellow sulfur) carries acyl groups. Acetyl-CoA is the crossroads of metabolism: carbohydrates, fats and amino acids all converge on it. Deficiency is almost never seen (“burning feet” in prisoners of war).
<b>Витамин B6.</b> Активная форма — <b>п: Vitamin B6. Its active form is pyridoxal phosphate: its aldehyde group (C=O) latches onto the amino group of an amino acid. It is the coenzyme of transaminases (ALT, AST), decarboxylases (synthesis of GABA, serotonin, histamine, dopamine) and heme synthesis. Deficiency: seizures in infants, dermatitis, anemia; it can occur during tuberculosis treatment with isoniazid. Sources: meat, fish, bananas, grains.
<b>Биотин (витамин H, B7)</b> пришиваетс: Biotin (vitamin H, B7) is attached to a lysine of carboxylases and carries CO₂: pyruvate carboxylase (gluconeogenesis), acetyl-CoA carboxylase (fat synthesis). Gut bacteria make a lot of it. Deficiency occurs when eating raw eggs: the egg-white protein avidin binds biotin irreversibly (dermatitis, hair loss).
<b>Фолиевая кислота</b> (лат. folium — л: Folic acid (Latin folium — leaf). Its reduced form, tetrahydrofolate, carries one-carbon groups for the synthesis of purines and thymidine — without it DNA cannot be replicated. Deficiency: megaloblastic anemia, and in the fetus, neural tube defects, so it is prescribed when planning a pregnancy. Methotrexate (the “Active form” button) is its structural analog, an anticancer drug. Sources: leafy greens, liver, legumes.
<b>Витамин B12 (кобаламин)</b> — самый с: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the most complex vitamin; at the center of its corrin ring is a cobalt atom (pink). Its coenzymes methylcobalamin and deoxyadenosylcobalamin are needed for methionine synthesis and for converting methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA. It is absorbed only together with Castle’s intrinsic factor from the stomach. Deficiency: pernicious anemia and spinal cord damage. It is found only in animal products — vegans need supplements. (The core of the molecule is shown without the long side tail.)
<b>Витамин C</b> — восстановитель и анти: Vitamin C is a reducing agent and antioxidant. It is needed by prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases, which finish making collagen: without vitamin C, collagen is weak. It helps iron absorption. Deficiency causes scurvy: bleeding gums, tooth loss, poor wound healing. Unlike most animals, humans cannot synthesize it. Sources: rose hips, blackcurrants, sweet peppers, citrus fruits.
<b>Витамин A (ретинол).</b> Его альдегид: Vitamin A (retinol). Its aldehyde, 11-cis-retinal, is the light-sensitive part of rhodopsin (“Vision” mode), and retinoic acid controls the genes for epithelial growth. Deficiency: “night blindness” (poor twilight vision), dry eyes and skin. Its provitamin is the β-carotene of carrots. Excess is toxic (liver, fetus). Sources: liver, fish oil, butter.
<b>Витамин D3 (холекальциферол)</b> обра: Vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) is formed in the skin under ultraviolet light from a cholesterol derivative. The liver adds OH at position 25 and the kidneys at position 1, giving the hormone calcitriol (the “Active form” button), which increases intestinal absorption of calcium and phosphate. Deficiency: rickets in children, osteomalacia in adults. Sources: sunlight, oily fish, eggs.
<b>Витамин E (токоферол)</b> — главный а: Vitamin E (tocopherol) is the main antioxidant of membranes. Its long tail hides among the fatty acids, while the ring with its OH group donates a hydrogen atom to a free radical and stops the lipid peroxidation chain reaction. Deficiency: red blood cell breakdown, muscle weakness, neuropathy. Sources: vegetable oils, nuts, seeds.
<b>Витамин K</b> нужен ферменту, который: Vitamin K is needed by the enzyme that converts glutamate residues into γ-carboxyglutamate in clotting factors II, VII, IX and X: only then can they bind calcium and work. Deficiency causes bleeding; newborns are given vitamin K. Warfarin (the “Active form” button) is a vitamin K antagonist, a drug against blood clots. Sources: green leaves (K1), gut bacteria (K2).
<b>НАД⁺ в работе.</b> Слева — вся молеку: NAD⁺ at work. On the left is the whole NAD⁺ molecule: adenosine, two phosphates and nicotinamide (vitamin PP), the working part. In the active site of a dehydrogenase (here lactate dehydrogenase), a hydride ion H⁻ (two electrons and a proton, yellow light) is pulled off lactate and lands on the nicotinamide ring: NAD⁺ → NADH, and the ring loses its aromaticity. The second proton goes into solution. Lactate becomes pyruvate. The graph shows why this is convenient to measure: NADH absorbs light at 340 nm, while NAD⁺ does not (Warburg’s optical test — this is how laboratories measure enzyme activity).
<b>Витамин A в зрении.</b> Реальная стру: Vitamin A in vision. The real structure of rhodopsin (PDB 1U19), the protein of retinal rods: seven helices span the membrane. In the middle of the bundle lies 11-cis-retinal (the aldehyde of vitamin A). A photon straightens it into the all-trans form within 200 femtoseconds — the protein changes shape and starts the cascade transducin → phosphodiesterase → closure of sodium channels. Then retinal detaches and is regenerated — this requires vitamin A; when it is lacking, twilight vision suffers (“night blindness”).
Тринадцать веществ, которые организм не: Thirteen substances the body cannot make on its own. Most of them are parts of enzymes: without the vitamin, the enzyme does not work.
\n <div><h2>Что такое витамины</h2>:
What vitamins are

Vitamins are low-molecular-weight organic substances needed in small amounts (micrograms to milligrams per day). They provide no energy and are not building material, but many of them are coenzyme precursors. Humans do not synthesize them, or do not synthesize enough.

Water-soluble vitamins (the B group and C) are not stored (except B12), so they must be obtained constantly. Fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) are absorbed together with fats and stored in the liver and adipose tissue — so an overdose is possible (hypervitaminosis A and D).

Disorders

Avitaminosis is a complete absence, hypovitaminosis a deficiency, hypervitaminosis an excess. Causes: a poor diet, impaired absorption, increased need (pregnancy, growth), suppression of the gut flora by antibiotics, and antivitamins — competing substances (methotrexate against B9, warfarin against K, avidin against biotin, isoniazid against B6).

<b>Механическая работа.</b> Головка миоз: Mechanical work. The myosin head hydrolyzes ATP and “rows” along the actin filament. A running muscle uses up its entire ATP store in a couple of seconds — after that it is replenished by creatine phosphate, glycolysis and the mitochondria.
<b>Осмотическая работа.</b> Na⁺/K⁺-АТФаз: Osmotic work. For each ATP, the Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase pumps 3 Na⁺ out of the cell and 2 K⁺ in. This takes up to a quarter of all resting energy, and in neurons up to two thirds.
<b>Химическая работа.</b> Анаболизм — си: Chemical work. Anabolism — the synthesis of proteins, nucleic acids, glycogen and fats — runs “uphill” (ΔG > 0) and becomes possible only when coupled to the hydrolysis of ATP (or GTP, UTP, CTP).
<b>Окислительное фосфорилирование</b> —: Oxidative phosphorylation is the main route (≈90% of ATP): the energy from oxidizing NADH and FADH₂ in the mitochondrial respiratory chain creates a proton gradient that spins ATP synthase.
<b>Субстратное фосфорилирование</b> — фо: Substrate-level phosphorylation: phosphate is transferred to ADP directly from an energy-rich molecule — 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate and phosphoenolpyruvate in glycolysis, succinyl-CoA in the Krebs cycle. It works even without oxygen.
<b>Стадия 1 — распад полимеров до мономе: Stage 1 — breakdown of polymers into monomers (in the gut and lysosomes): proteins → amino acids, polysaccharides → glucose, fats → glycerol and fatty acids. Little energy is released (<1%), and it is dissipated as heat.
<b>Стадия 2 — свои пути для каждого клас: Stage 2 — separate pathways for each class (cytoplasm and mitochondria): glycolysis, β-oxidation of fatty acids, deamination of amino acids. They all converge on one substance — acetyl-CoA. About a third of the energy is released; some ATP is formed by substrate-level phosphorylation.
<b>Стадия 3 — общий путь катаболизма</b>: Stage 3 — the common pathway of catabolism in the mitochondria: the tricarboxylic acid cycle oxidizes acetyl-CoA to 2 CO₂, and hydrogen carried by NADH and FADH₂ enters the respiratory chain, where it combines with oxygen to form water. About two thirds of all the energy is released here, and most of the ATP is formed.
<b>АТФ — энергетическая валюта клетки.</: ATP is the energy currency of the cell. Adenine, ribose and three phosphates; the bonds between the phosphates are high-energy bonds: hydrolysis of the terminal phosphate releases 30.5 kJ/mol. Watch the cycle: water attacks the bond, a phosphate (Pi) breaks off, and the energy goes to work — muscular, transport or chemical. Then ADP is “recharged” using the oxidation of nutrients. The graph shows ATP in the middle of the high-energy scale: it can receive phosphate from richer molecules (PEP, 1,3-BPG, creatine phosphate) and give it to poorer ones (glucose → glucose-6-phosphate).
<b>Три стадии катаболизма.</b> Сотни раз: Three stages of catabolism. Hundreds of different food molecules converge into a few common pathways: proteins, carbohydrates and fats are broken down to monomers, the monomers to acetyl-CoA, and acetyl-CoA is burned in the Krebs cycle and the respiratory chain to CO₂ and water, producing ATP. The nitrogen of amino acids leaves as ammonia (and then as urea). Click a stage.

\n <div><h2>Энергия в клетке</h2>\n:
Energy in the cell

Metabolism = catabolism (breakdown, ΔG < 0, exergonic reactions) + anabolism (synthesis, ΔG > 0, endergonic). They are linked by coupling: the energy of breakdown is stored in high-energy compounds (ATP) and reduced coenzymes (NADH, NADPH, FADH₂) and spent on synthesis and work.

Change in free energy: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. If ΔG < 0, the reaction proceeds spontaneously; if ΔG > 0, only when paired with an energy-yielding reaction.

How ATP is made

Oxidative phosphorylation (mitochondria, ~90%) and substrate-level phosphorylation (glycolysis, Krebs cycle). Muscles have a fast reserve — creatine phosphate: creatine kinase transfers its phosphate to ADP in a fraction of a second.

Stages of metabolism

  1. Intake with food.
  2. Digestion to monomers.
  3. Absorption and transport in blood and lymph.
  4. Intermediary metabolism in cells.
  5. Excretion of end products: CO₂, H₂O, urea.

Models

  • Molecules are built from their chemical formulas; the protein in the funnel is lysozyme (PDB 1AKI), as an example of a protein.
  • The “energy packet” is a convention: energy is transferred through a chemical bond, it does not fly through the air.

<b>1. Цитратсинтаза</b> соединяет ацетил: 1. Citrate synthase joins acetyl-CoA (C2) to oxaloacetate (C4), giving six-carbon citrate and releasing HS-CoA. The energy comes from breaking the thioester bond. It is inhibited by ATP, NADH, succinyl-CoA and citrate itself.
<b>2. Аконитаза</b> через цис-аконитат (: 2. Aconitase, via cis-aconitate (removing and then re-adding water), moves the OH group: citrate → isocitrate. The enzyme contains an iron–sulfur cluster. It is blocked by fluorocitrate, which is formed from fluoroacetate (a rat poison).
<b>3. Изоцитратдегидрогеназа</b> окисляе: 3. Isocitrate dehydrogenase oxidizes isocitrate and removes CO₂, giving five-carbon α-ketoglutarate and the first NADH. This is the main regulatory enzyme of the cycle: it is activated by ADP and Ca²⁺ and inhibited by ATP and NADH.
<b>4. α-Кетоглутаратдегидрогеназный комп: 4. The α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex is built like pyruvate dehydrogenase (the same 5 coenzymes: TPP, lipoic acid, CoA, FAD, NAD⁺). The second oxidative decarboxylation yields CO₂, NADH and the high-energy compound succinyl-CoA. It is blocked by arsenite.
<b>5. Сукцинил-КоА-синтетаза (сукцинилти: 5. Succinyl-CoA synthetase (succinate thiokinase): the energy of the thioester bond is used to make GTP from GDP and phosphate — this is substrate-level phosphorylation. GTP passes its phosphate to ADP → ATP.
<b>6. Сукцинатдегидрогеназа</b> снимает: 6. Succinate dehydrogenase removes two hydrogen atoms and passes them to FAD → FADH₂, giving fumarate with a double bond. It is the only enzyme of the cycle embedded in the inner membrane: it is complex II of the respiratory chain. Its competitive inhibitor is malonate (button below).
<b>7. Фумараза</b> присоединяет воду по: 7. Fumarase adds water across the double bond: fumarate → L-malate.
<b>8. Малатдегидрогеназа</b> окисляет ма: 8. Malate dehydrogenase oxidizes malate to oxaloacetate, producing the third NADH. The circle is closed: oxaloacetate is ready to accept the next acetyl-CoA.
